note: Medical Terminology Only In Finals pictures, built with /workspace/study-images/work (cfg.py, build.py); image paths point at the portal copies.

images.title: Lobes of the Brain
images.caption: The cerebrum (Cerebr/o) is divided into the frontal, parietal, temporal and occipital lobes. The cerebellum (Cerebell/o) sits at the back and coordinates balance and movement.
images.alt: Side view of the brain with each lobe in a different colour: frontal, parietal, temporal and occipital lobes, plus the cerebellum and brainstem.
images.credit: Cancer Research UK, via Wikimedia Commons

images.title: The Meninges
images.caption: Mening/o means membrane. The three meninges cover the brain and spinal cord: the tough dura mater on the outside, the arachnoid in the middle, and the delicate pia mater on the brain surface.
images.alt: Cut-away from the scalp down to the brain showing the skin, aponeurosis, periosteum and bone, then the dura mater, arachnoid and pia mater, with a dural venous sinus and an arachnoid granulation.
images.credit: Mysid (SVG), SEER Development Team (original), Jmarchn, via Wikimedia Commons

images.title: Brain: Midsagittal View
images.caption: The thalamus (Thalam/o) relays sensory signals, and the hypothalamus below it controls body temperature, hunger and hormones. The brainstem (midbrain, pons and medulla oblongata) connects the brain to the spinal cord (Myel/o).
images.alt: Brain cut down the middle showing the cerebrum, corpus callosum, thalamus, hypothalamus, cerebellum and the highlighted brainstem: mesencephalon, pons and medulla oblongata, continuing into the spinal cord.
images.credit: Patrick J. Lynch, variation by User:Hk kng, via Wikimedia Commons

images.title: Brain: Deep Structures (Midsagittal Cut)
images.caption: Cut close to the midline, the corpus callosum arches over the thalamus, the relay centre for sensory signals (Thalam/o). The hypothalamus lies below and in front of it and controls hormones, temperature and hunger, and the small pineal gland sits behind it and releases melatonin.
images.alt: Human Atlas render of the brain cut lengthways close to the midline, front to the left: the corpus callosum (blue arch), thalamus (purple), hypothalamus (yellow) and pineal gland (red), with the cerebrum, brainstem and cerebellum in muted colours.
images.credit: Rendered from BodyParts3D 4.0 (DBCLS) via Human Atlas

images.title: Structure of a Neuron
images.caption: Neur/o means nerve. A neuron receives signals through its dendrites, and the cell body (with its nucleus) passes them along the axon to the axon terminals. Schwann cells form the myelin sheath that speeds the signal.
images.alt: A neuron with branching dendrites, a cell body with its nucleus, and a long axon wrapped in myelin sheath segments formed by Schwann cells, separated by nodes of Ranvier, ending in axon terminals.

images.title: Central vs Peripheral Nervous System
images.caption: The central nervous system (CNS) is the brain (Encephal/o) and spinal cord (Myel/o). The peripheral nervous system (PNS) is the nerves and ganglia (clusters of nerve cell bodies) that connect the CNS to the rest of the body.
images.alt: Body outline showing the brain and spinal cord as the central nervous system, and nerves and ganglia branching out as the peripheral nervous system.

images.title: The Cerebrum
images.caption: The cerebrum has two hemispheres, each with frontal, parietal, temporal and occipital lobes. Its folds are gyri and the grooves between them are sulci.
images.alt: Side view of the brain with the four lobes coloured, and a top view showing the two hemispheres.

images.title: The Large Intestine
images.caption: The large intestine starts at the cecum (the blind pouch), where the ileum joins it through the ileocecal valve. The worm-like appendix hangs from the cecum. The colon (Col/o, Colon/o) runs up (ascending), across (transverse), down (descending) and through the S-shaped sigmoid colon to the rectum (Rect/o) and anus (An/o).
images.alt: Front view of the large intestine: the ileum entering the cecum at the ileocecal valve, the appendix, the ascending, transverse, descending and sigmoid colon, the rectum and the anus, with a small body outline showing where it sits.
images.credit: Blausen.com staff (2014), "Medical gallery of Blausen Medical 2014", WikiJournal of Medicine, via Wikimedia Commons

images.title: Liver, Gallbladder and Bile Ducts
images.caption: The liver (Hepat/o) makes bile (Bil/i, Chol/e). The gallbladder stores it and sends it down the cystic duct, which joins the hepatic duct to form the common bile duct into the duodenum. The pancreas (Pancreat/o) adds its juice through the pancreatic duct.
images.alt: The liver with its bile ducts, the gallbladder, the cystic duct and common bile duct, and the pancreas with the pancreatic duct, drawn over the esophagus, stomach and small intestine.

images.title: Kidney Anatomy
images.caption: Nephr/o and Ren/o mean kidney. The outer cortex (bark) holds the nephrons, the medulla holds the renal pyramids, and urine drains into the renal pelvis (Pyel/o) and down the ureter (Ureter/o). The renal artery, renal vein and ureter pass through the hilum.
images.alt: A kidney cut open showing the renal cortex, renal medulla with its pyramids, columns, papillae and calyces, the renal pelvis and ureter, and the renal artery and vein at the hilum, with a small body outline showing where the kidneys sit.
images.credit: Blausen.com staff (2014), "Medical gallery of Blausen Medical 2014", WikiJournal of Medicine, via Wikimedia Commons

images.title: Male Reproductive System
images.caption: Sperm (Sperm/o, Spermat/o) are made in the testis (Orchi/o, Orchid/o, Test/o), mature in the epididymis (Epididym/o), and travel up the vas deferens (Vas/o) to the ejaculatory duct and urethra. The seminal vesicle, prostate gland (Prostat/o) and bulbourethral gland add fluid to make semen.
images.alt: Side view of the male pelvis cut down the middle, showing the urinary bladder, vas deferens, seminal vesicle, ejaculatory duct, prostate gland, bulbourethral gland, urethra, penis with glans and external urethral orifice, epididymis, testis and scrotum.

images.title: Female Reproductive System
images.caption: The ovaries (Ovari/o, Oophor/o) make eggs and female hormones. The fallopian (uterine) tubes (Salping/o) carry the egg to the uterus (Hyster/o, Metr/o, Uter/o). The cervix (Cervic/o) joins the uterus to the vagina (Vagin/o, Colp/o), and the vulva (Vulv/o) is the external genitalia.
images.alt: Front view of the female pelvis showing the two ovaries, the fallopian tubes, the uterus, the cervix, the vagina and the vulva, set between the hip bones.
